newsitem.title: USA: Clinton refuses to hand over Haiti papers - report.
newsitem.headline: Clinton refuses to hand over Haiti papers - report.

text.p: President Bill Clinton invoked executive privilege and refused to hand over documents subpoenaed by a Congressional panel probing alleged U.S. efforts to conceal activities of Haitian death squads in 1994, The Washington Post reported on Thursday.
The newspaper quoted from a letter written by White House counsel Jack Quinn which said the subpoena went too far.

"The documents requested include memoranda of conversations with a foreign president and prime minister, memoranda to the president and vice president and memoranda relating to the deliberations of the president's most senior National Security Council staff," Quinn wrote.
The White House believed that releasing them would undermine the confidence of foreign leaders and senior aides that their conversations with the president would remain confidential, the Post said.

Benjamin Gilman, chairman of the House of Representatives International Relations Committee, who issued the subpoena last week said a year-long inquiry by his committee into political murders in Haiti had been spurred by the apparent re-emergence of death squads run by the U.S.-backed government in Port-au-Prince.

Gilman, a New York Republican, said he believed the documents would disclose information about administration efforts to conceal death squads run by key aides of former President Jean-Bertrand Aristide beginning shortly after the U.S. military intervention in Haiti in 1994.
Aristide was overthrown in a 1991 military coup and restored to power by the U.S. intervention.

Last week the administration sent about 40 State Department security agents to Haiti amid allegations that members of current President Rene Preval's personal security unit were involved in two killings.
